body:
Eric Watt Forste <arkuat@pobox.com> wrote:
> Nietzsche confronted nineteenth-century Europe's social problems with a
> thoughtful analysis, which was ignored during his working lifetime. He
> had the patience to wait for his ideas to come into circulation, as they
> eventually did. 

But even today, few people understand Nietzsche, even among those 
philosophers that attempt to study him.  I think it's safe to say that
he's still ignored by those who need him most and could implement his
ideas best.

> He lacked the arrogance of FC, who wants to further
> people's happiness by blowing them up, who wants to shove his own values
> down our throats at gunpoint. Nietzsche's ideas aren't even all that
> dated, and they are *far* less simplistic than FC's.

Nietzsche was fighting a different battle than FC, so it's not really
a fair comparison.  Time also is important here.  People are getting
dumber today and are swarmed with "information" from newspapers, TVs,
and radio.  As FC wrote in paragraph 96 of the Manifesto:

[...] Take us (FC) for example.  If we had never done anything violent
      and had submitted the present writings to a publisher, they
      probably would not have been accepted.  If they had been accepted
      and published, they probably would not have attracted many
      readers, because it's more fun to watch the entertainment put
      out by the media than to read a sober essay.  Even if these
      writings had had many readers, most of these readers would
      soon have forgotten what they had read as their minds were 
      flooded by the mass of material to which the media expose them.  
      In order to get our message before the public with some change of
      making a lasting impression, we've had to kill people.

> FC's ideas are based on 1) questionable assertions about how much
> control individuals had over their own lives in preindustrial society
> and 

What is questionable?  If people didn't like it, they could go somewhere
else easily.  There's very much involved today with attempting to move
from one area to another and subservience to many systems that have
to be interfaced with.

> 2) an utterly spurious distinction between "real" goals and
> "surrogate" goals. FC's "real" goals are just those goals that happen to
> have been hardwired into our nervous and hormonal systems as a result of
> a long series of evolutionary accidents (but then again, FC seems to
> worship pure random Chance--which he sometimes calls Nature--as a god),
> and FC's "surrogate" goals are those that individuals choose for
> themselves, rather than have imposed on them by the brute fact of their
> genetic heritage. Which of these two sets sounds more compatible with
> human freedom to you?

Real goals are related to actions that brought the human this far in
his chain of existence.  Surrogate goals are actions that take up time
to keep people from boredom and have little or no other value.  When
you need surrogate goals, that is an indication that you are not free
and are seeking distractions because of your unnatural state of living.

>> He's not a coward.
>
> He lacked the courage to fight for his ideals the hard way, by working
> to draw people's attention to them on their own merits (which are slim),
> and slipped into the easy, lazy, and cowardly way: making people pay
> attention to them by threatening to kill them if they didn't.

Except no one today cares about the society and environment around them.
They just work obediently for meager rewards and trade away their
lives to companies for little in return.  Don't you understand the
negative response to his message?  People hate having their meaningless
lives exposed when they aren't willing to do something about it.  They
are embarrassed that their petty values and worthlessness has been
brought in the open, and they love being basically high wage slaves.

>> You're just repeating what the media is telling
>> you to think, aren't you?  You shouldn't let them control your mind,
>> presuming that you still have one.
>
> Do you repeat this to everyone whose view is different from yours?

No.  You are just repeating the oversocialized media position though,
which indicates that you have not thought very much about this.

>> Why not benefit mankind by implementing his ideas and letting him
>> discuss them further?
>
> Who exactly is preventing the further discussion of his ideas?

If the Unabomber is Ted, then the FBI is preventing him from further
discussion of his ideas.  The Unabomber had intended to have follow-ups
to the Manifesto published so the revolutionaries could be more accurate
in their actions.

> I don't feel particularly impaired, myself, right now as I discuss his 
> ideas with you. 

Except that I would question whether or not you understand anything more
than what the media has told you to think.

> How would you like to go about implementing his ideas?

Wide scale revolution.  But few people have the time and brainpower to
even read his Manifesto, so I think mankind is already doomed into
devolution.  We'll be very much like the apes in a few hundred years.

>> We're in alt.fan.unabomber to start the revolution and take back our 
>> freedom from the enslavers.
>
> It's a lot more effective to think about your own freedom and how to
> best attain and enhance it. If everyone did this for themselves, there
> would be no need for revolutions and violence (not that there's any need
> anyway). Rework your own life before you go around threatening to kill
> other people unless they rework theirs.

I am thinking about my own freedom and to best attack the systems that 
limit it, it is most effective to work with others who have the same
goals of breaking these systems.  The Manifesto provided the crack and
now we must drive the wedge to break the system completely apart.

However, I do not believe that the same social scum (foresters, polluters,
advertising/marketing executives) will at any point begin to respect
the freedom of others when they can instead exploit them of their
environment.  Therefore action is needed against these sort of people
for the benefit of self and others.

-Ric
